title: Microfluidics for single-cell lineage tracking over time to characterize transmission of phenotypes in Saccharomyces cerevisiae
protocol: Inoculate 3 mL synthetic media in a 15-mL tube with yeast from a freshly streaked plate.
Grow the inoculated yeast cultures at 30°C with shaking at 250–300 rpm for 10–15 hours.
Filter media through a 0.22 μm filter to remove particulate matter or precipitates.
Inoculate a fresh culture of 3 mL media with 25-50 μL culture from the first step.
Grow the new inoculated cultures at 30°C with shaking at 250–300 rpm for approximately 4 hours until cells reach low log phase.
Place microfluidics chip in the heating chip holder.
Secure the microfluidics chip with screws and holders.
Secure the chip tightly on the stage to prevent movement during the time-lapse experiment.
Connect all tubings for media and cell inlets and outlets to the chip.
Prime the chip and tubings with medium until continuous flow is observed into the waste.
Inject cells from a low log phase culture into each microchamber using a 1 mL syringe and a 22 gauge blunt edge needle.
Start pumping media through chip.
Choose positions to image.
Set focus for each position.
Collect images with 3-min resolution with phase contrast and any filters for fluorescent molecules of interest.
Acquire images in the following order: (channel 1) phase contrast, (channel 2) fluorescent protein of interest, (channel 3) lineage marker.
Segment cells using fluorescence or phase contrast images.
Import images into PhyloCell to generate a segmentation project.
Convert ND2 files into JPEG images for use in PhyloCell (optional).
Map cells so that they are tracked from frame to frame.
Build pedigrees based on mother-bud proximity or lineage markers.
Correct any errors in segmentation, mapping, or lineage tracking.
Measure fluorescence in segmented cells.
Subtract cellular autofluorescence and/or background fluorescence.
